review.summary: Packet-only review of two debugger readers, two hardened launchers, the e2e-reviewer scanner, and two skill contracts. Agreement between the playwright-debugger SKILL.md and read-playwright-artifact.py is unusually tight: every documented ceiling (8 MiB report, 64 MiB archive/image, 512 MiB video, 100 depth, 200,000 nodes, 10,000 records, 100 attempts, 1 MiB output, 10,000 ZIP entries, 200:1 ratio, 32 MiB selected entry), every mode (report/trace/media/trace-snapshot), the --report-root requirement, the descriptor-identity recheck, the nested-then-legacy errorLocation fallback, and the synthetic global/project error records are all present in code as documented. Both launchers implement the same closed --pass-env allowlists the docs describe (readers none, publisher PATH, downloader HOME/GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN), select an interpreter only from a fixed absolute candidate list, and exec through env -i. scan.sh separates confirmed P0 from LLM-triage and unproven-provenance candidates, proves framework lineage through a shared lexer rather than filename convention, revalidates a SHA-256 candidate manifest between tiers, and fails closed (exit 2, no Summary) on tier infrastructure failure, output-limit trips, and root-identity drift. Defects found are bounded: the report reader re-derives Playwright outcome classification and hard-fails the whole report on any disagreement with the reporter's own status; the playwright-debugger doc mandates an empty-environment wrapper for every repository-controlled command but omits it from its own Phase 2 probe; playwright-test-generator uses an undefined $SKILL_ROOT in three executable snippets; the Cypress reader lacks the sibling reader's post-serialization residual-credential gate and finite-float parse guard; the scanner's mode-bit check feeds a possibly-octal string to decimal arithmetic; the preflight symlink abort has no documented override; and JUSTIFIED-suppressed P0s escape the default exit gate. No critical or high findings. Verdict is FAIL only because the weighted overall score falls under the fixed 90 threshold, not because of any blocking finding.

findings.title: Reader re-derives Playwright outcome and rejects the whole report on any disagreement
findings.evidence: Line 742 classifies an `interrupted` result as `unexpected` inside computed_test_outcome, and line 822 raises whenever the reporter's own `test.status` differs from that recomputation. Because the raise happens during report_specs traversal, a single disagreeing test aborts the entire read: no records, no synthetic error records, no stats. The reader therefore hard-depends on tracking the runner's internal outcome derivation across versions, and the all-or-nothing failure lands exactly on interrupted/aborted runs (SIGINT, maxFailures) that users most need to diagnose.
findings.recommendation: Keep the recomputation as a per-test advisory field (e.g. `computedOutcome`) and restrict the hard failure to structurally invalid records, so a classification divergence degrades one record instead of refusing the whole artifact.

findings.title: Phase 2 isolation probe omits the empty-environment wrapper the same document mandates
findings.evidence: Lines 111-113 state that every repository-controlled command below must run with an explicit empty environment, shown as `/usr/bin/env -i PATH="$PATH"`, and the Prerequisites repro snippets at lines 244 and 248 comply. The Phase 2 F1-vs-F7 probe at line 367 (and its companion at line 371) invokes `npx --no-install playwright test ...` with no wrapper, so ambient credentials and injection variables such as NODE_OPTIONS reach project-controlled config, reporters, and fixtures. Line 371 additionally runs the full suite with no spec filter despite the execution-safety gate at lines 129-133 requiring the narrowest spec.
findings.recommendation: Prefix both probe commands with `/usr/bin/env -i PATH="$PATH"` and state explicitly that command (b) is a whole-suite run requiring the disposable-target gate.

findings.title: Permission-bit check uses decimal arithmetic on a string bash may parse as octal
findings.evidence: Line 51 accepts any all-digit mode string from file_mode, and line 52 extracts the group digit with `$(((mode / 10) % 10))`. Bash arithmetic treats a leading `0` as an octal literal, so a stat implementation emitting `0770` evaluates as 504, yielding group_digit 0 and other_digit 4 — both of which pass the not-group/other-writable tests on lines 54-57. A group-writable interpreter path would then be accepted as a root-owned system path. The identical code exists at skills/cypress-debugger/scripts/run-artifact-reader.sh line 52.
findings.recommendation: Normalize the mode with `mode=${mode#"${mode%%[!0]*}"}` (or compare digits with string indexing instead of arithmetic) in both launchers before the group/other checks.

findings.title: Cypress emit path has no post-serialization residual-credential backstop
findings.evidence: emit_json calls redact_for_output at line 922, then validates shape and only enforces a byte ceiling at line 931 before printing. The sibling reader's encode_json re-runs the redactor and fails closed on non-idempotence (read-playwright-artifact.py line 1309) and rescans the serialized payload with has_residual_credential (line 1319). The Cypress output gate is therefore only as strong as a redactor module that is not included in this packet, with no independent fail-closed check on the bytes actually emitted.
findings.recommendation: Mirror the Playwright pattern: re-apply the redactor and compare for idempotence, and run a residual-credential scan over the encoded payload before printing.

findings.title: Strict JSON decoder omits the finite-float guard used by the sibling reader
findings.evidence: The JSONDecoder configured at lines 105-108 sets object_pairs_hook and parse_constant but no parse_float, whereas read-playwright-artifact.py line 148 installs `parse_float=parse_finite_float`. Literals such as `1e999` therefore decode to `float('inf')` and survive parsing; they are only caught incidentally later by `allow_nan=False` at serialization or by range comparisons such as the percent check at lines 356-360. Two readers documented and built as siblings apply different strictness to the same untrusted-JSON trust boundary.
findings.recommendation: Add the same `parse_float` finite guard (and a matching parse_int bound if desired) to the Cypress decoder so non-finite numbers are rejected at parse time.

findings.title: Executable snippets use an undefined $SKILL_ROOT
findings.evidence: Line 122 assigns `write_frame="$SKILL_ROOT/scripts/write-utf8-frame.sh"`, and lines 128, 213, and 214 invoke launchers through the same variable, but no included line defines $SKILL_ROOT or states how to resolve it. The companion skill does define its placeholder explicitly (skills/playwright-debugger/SKILL.md line 265: resolve <skill-dir> as the directory containing this SKILL.md). The same snippet also expands $TARGET_URL and $BASE_URL at lines 124-125 before either is assigned anywhere in the document; TARGET_URL is first set only at line 211.
findings.recommendation: Add one sentence defining $SKILL_ROOT as the absolute directory containing this SKILL.md, and set TARGET_URL/BASE_URL in the preflight snippet as it is set in the later ARIA-fallback snippet.

findings.title: Preflight symlink abort has no documented override, so one link disables the whole review
findings.evidence: preflight_scanner_tree exits 2 with 'no scan was run' whenever special_entry_can_hide_scanner_source matches any entry — which per lines 1840-1856 includes every symlink carrying one of the eight code extensions, every directory symlink, and broken symlinks named src/test/tests/e2e/spec/specs/playwright/cypress/support/fixtures. Vendor trees are pruned, but an ordinary workspace link such as packages/app/src -> ../../shared/src aborts the entire scan before any tier runs. None of the ~15 E2E_SMELL_* knobs validated at lines 242-342 provides an override or allowlist, and the message names the entries without stating a remediation.
findings.recommendation: Keep the default fail-closed behavior but add an explicit opt-in (for example an E2E_SMELL_ALLOW_SYMLINK_PATHS allowlist, echoed into the Summary as reduced coverage) and print the remediation in the INCOMPLETE message.

findings.title: Default exit gate ignores JUSTIFIED-suppressed P0 candidates
findings.evidence: The default gate (FAIL_ON defaults to p0 at line 8) tests only `unique_p0_hits` at line 5919. Lines 5405-5420 route any non-#7 P0 whose line carries a `// JUSTIFIED:` comment through record_justified_suppression, and lines 5839-5844 add those to `p0_candidate_hits`, which only the opt-in `p0-candidate` arm at lines 5921-5923 evaluates. A repository that controls both the test and the comment can therefore convert a build-failing silent-pass P0 (#4f, #3) into a non-failing, merely-printed candidate. The deliberate #7 carve-out at line 5405 shows the risk is understood for focused tests but not generalized.
findings.recommendation: Make `p0-candidate` the default value of E2E_SMELL_FAIL_ON, or require JUSTIFIED suppressions to name an external verification reference before they leave the failing bucket.

limitations: Zero-tool, packet-only review: nothing was executed, so all scoring is contract and design analysis, not observed behavior.

Load-bearing dependencies are omitted and were treated as unverifiable, not as passing: residual_credentials.py, redact_artifact.py, publish-json-report.py, download-playwright-report.py, extract-junit-failures.py, publish-mochawesome-report.py, download-cypress-reports.py, write-utf8-frame.sh, run-preflight-target.sh, run-raw-aria-snapshot.sh, the ast-grep-rules directory, and parse-ast-grep-json.py.
No SKILL.md is included for e2e-reviewer or cypress-debugger, so their invocation, knob, and exit-code contracts could only be read out of code comments in scan.sh and the launcher.
No tests, fixtures, CI harness, or evaluation corpus are included; the verification_design score reflects only the fail-closed structure visible in the included scripts.

Framework-semantics judgments about Playwright's own outcome derivation rest on model knowledge, not on included runner source; the cited finding is therefore framed around the all-or-nothing failure mode, which the included lines prove independently.
Byte-level equivalence of the two run-artifact-reader.sh launchers was assessed by reading, not by diffing; the shared mode-arithmetic defect is reported once with the sibling path named.

This is a fresh-context review of a curated contract/implementation subset in a Claude-only completion of the preregistered v10 schedule, designed after observing the carried v10 attempt's valid FAIL; it is not unbiased defect discovery, remediation confirmation, cross-provider evidence, full product coverage, or skill accuracy.
Under the FAIL-first rule the carried v10 attempt already fixes any completed aggregate as FAIL; this attempt is a completion and descriptive observation and cannot change that gate.
The packet, prompt, rubric, remediation ledger, model catalog, and pinned CLI are inherited byte-for-byte from the frozen v10 archive; only the harness differs from the carried attempt.
The public packet is not human or sealed review, independent ground truth, or remote model attestation.
The local UUIDv4 invocation ID separates runner invocations but cannot attest that a distinct remote model call occurred.

This phase runs two Anthropic models, claude-opus-5 twice and claude-fable-5 once. Model coverage is deliberately unbalanced, so no per-model rate is claimed; the aggregate requires every attempt to pass. Both models share one provider family, so this is not cross-provider evidence.

Prompt size is measured in exact UTF-8 bytes and a pinned OpenAI o200k_base reference count used only as a deterministic size proxy. That count is not the model's own tokenization, and no local source establishes a context window for these models, so no context-window fit is claimed.
Excluded scorecards, holdouts, reports, prior reviews, chat conclusions, and git history reduce but cannot prove absence of training-data contamination.
